info.title: Record White Collar API
info.description: Run Record white-collar assessments from your own system: set up a job, have Record write the assessment, invite candidates by email and receive their scores. You need two things: your **key id** and your **secret**. Everything else is generated. See Authentication for how.

tags.name: Lookups

tags.name: Questions

tags.name: Results

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Pull your result events and acknowledge them: the safety net behind the webhook, and a way to receive results without exposing a URL

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Endpoints that Record POSTs result events to: signed, retried until you acknowledge, replayable

post.summary: Create a job mandate under one of your workflows
post.description:
A job mandate is one role: its details and the assessment candidates sit (difficulty, which question types, how many, marks, pass mark, duration). It starts with no questions: write them with `POST /mandates/{mandate_id}/questions/generate` (Record's AI writes them from the job) or supply your own with `PUT /mandates/{mandate_id}/questions`. A campaign can be created once the questions are `ready`. The workflow must be a white-collar, recruiter-led one of your organisation.

**Scope:** `wc_mandates:write` · **Idempotency-Key:** optional

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key returns the first answer (kept 24 h). Leave empty in Try it: a new one is made for every call.

workflow_id.description: Record's white-collar workflow id (WF_WC_...): the workflow_id returned when you create the workflow

external_id.description: Your own job id. Unique among the mandates you created

experience.description: Experience wanted, in your words (e.g. 3 to 5 years)

job_description.description: The questions are written from this and the skills

skills.description: Skills the assessment should cover (up to 20)

count.description: How many questions of this type

marks_each.description: Marks for each question of this type

question_types.description: How many questions of which type, and the marks for each. Their sum is the total marks

total_marks.description: Optional: defaults to what the enabled question types add up to; if sent, it must equal that sum

pass_mark.description: The score that counts as a pass (verdict hire). Not above the total marks

duration_minutes.description: Minutes a candidate has to complete the assessment

is_external.description: true when the mandate was created through this API, false when it was made in the Record playground

404.description: `NOT_FOUND`: the workflow does not exist, or is not a white-collar one of yours.

patch.description:
Only the fields sent change; assessment fields merge one by one. Changing what the questions are written from (title, experience, description, skills, difficulty, question types) marks ready questions `outdated`: regenerate or re-save them before creating a campaign. post.description:
Record's AI writes the assessment from the job details and the assessment settings, replacing any questions the job had. The call waits for the questions and can take up to a minute: send an `Idempotency-Key` and, if it times out, retry with the same key. 502 means the questions could not be written; nothing changed, try again.

**Scope:** `wc_mandates:write` · **Idempotency-Key:** optional

post.summary: Create a campaign for one of your job mandates, and start it
post.description:
Invites candidates to the job's assessment by email: each gets a link to take it. The job's questions must be `ready` and the job open. `start: now` sends the invitations at once, in the background (the campaign reads `sending` until everyone has been reached); `start: manual` only creates it, start it later with `POST /campaigns/{id}/start`. This emails real people and spends credits, so it needs the `wc_campaigns:write` scope, an `Idempotency-Key`, and is capped per day. An organisation that cannot pay answers 402 before anything is created. An address that is invalid or repeated is returned in `rejected` with the reason; the rest go ahead.

**Scope:** `wc_campaigns:write` · **Idempotency-Key:** optional

> **This contacts real candidates.** Build against a TEST key first.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key returns the first answer (kept 24 h). Leave empty in Try it: a new one is made for every call.

mandate_id.description: Record's white-collar mandate id (wcm_...): the mandate_id returned when you create the mandate

name.description: Defaults to the job title and today's date

external_id.description: Your own id for this campaign. Must be unique

start.description: now: send straight away. manual: create a draft and start it later

external_id.description: Your own id for this candidate. Comes back on every result, so you can match it to your record

email.description: The address the assessment link is emailed to. A candidate is told apart by it, once per campaign

201.description: The campaign, how many candidates were accepted, and any that were left out

mandate_id.description: The job mandate this campaign runs under; null on a campaign made without one

status.description: draft: nobody has been invited. sending: started, and some candidates are still waiting for their invitation. sent: everyone has been reached (or failed: see candidates.failed). paused. completed. cancelled

failed.description: The invitation could not be delivered; starting the campaign again retries them

is_external.description: true when the campaign was created through this API, false when it was made in the Record playground

index.description: Position in the candidates you sent

rejected.description: Candidates left out and why. The rest went ahead

402.description: `INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS`: the organisation cannot pay for the invitations. Nothing was created or sent.

403.description: `FORBIDDEN`: this was made in the Record playground. The API reads it but changes only what it created.

404.description: `NOT_FOUND`: the job mandate does not exist.

409.description: `CONFLICT`: the job is closed, its questions are not `ready`, or `external_id` is already used.

429.description: `DAILY_CAP`: this key has put its daily allowance of different candidates into campaigns. Resets at midnight IST (see `Retry-After`).

post.summary: Add more candidates to a campaign you created
post.description:
On a campaign that has been sent, the newcomers are invited at once; on a draft or a paused campaign they wait until it is started or resumed. A candidate already in the campaign (same email) is left out and listed in `rejected`; nothing else is affected. At most 2000 candidates per campaign.

**Scope:** `wc_campaigns:write` · **Idempotency-Key:** optional

> **This contacts real candidates.** Build against a TEST key first.

post.summary: Start a campaign you created with start: manual
post.description:
Sends the invitations, in the background. Calling it on a campaign that was already sent retries the candidates whose invitation failed or never went out, and does nothing when everyone has been reached. 402 if the organisation cannot pay for the invitations still to go.

**Scope:** `wc_campaigns:write` · **Idempotency-Key:** optional

> **This contacts real candidates.** Build against a TEST key first.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key returns the first answer (kept 24 h). Leave empty in Try it: a new one is made for every call.

mandate_id.description: The job mandate this campaign runs under; null on a campaign made without one

status.description: draft: nobody has been invited. sending: started, and some candidates are still waiting for their invitation. sent: everyone has been reached (or failed: see candidates.failed). paused. completed. cancelled

failed.description: The invitation could not be delivered; starting the campaign again retries them

post.summary: Pull your result events and confirm the last ones
post.description:
The same `assessment.result` events the webhook sends, for pulling, in one call: send the `ack` ids of the events you processed from the previous call, and get the next page back. With the default `status=unacked` you get every event you have not acknowledged, oldest first, so one you missed or failed to process comes again. Loop: process the page, pass its ids as `ack` of the next call, repeat. A call whose response is lost loses nothing: its events were not acknowledged yet and come again. Acknowledging is safe to repeat (ids already acknowledged, or unknown, are accepted) and also closes a webhook delivery still waiting for them. `status=all` (with `from`) replays history; events are kept 30 days. `after` is only a paging shortcut: rely on `unacked`. An event is written once a candidate's attempt has ended (completed, timed out, disqualified, or the invitation failed) and its result has stayed the same for a short while.

**Scope:** `wc_events:read`

ack.description: Up to 100 ids of events you processed. They are acknowledged before the page is read, so they do not come back

from.description: Only events created at or after this time (replay)

after.description: Only events with a higher `sequence` than this

event_id.description: Stable forever. Keep the ones you processed and skip repeats

version.description: Rises each time the same candidate's result changes (a grade that lands later, a new attempt). Keep the highest

sequence.description: Order of events in your stream

backfill.description: true when the event was created for a webhook backfill

acknowledged.description: true once you acknowledged it (webhook 2xx, or listed in `ack` of POST /events/pull)

post.description:
Record sends every white-collar result event (`assessment.result`) to this URL and retries until you answer 2xx (about 52 hours, then the delivery is kept as dead and can be replayed). Each request is signed with your API secret key (VFN_SK_...), so there is no extra secret to keep. Registering a URL you already have returns that endpoint (`existing: true`), never a second one. At most 5 endpoints. `backfill_from` also sends results from the past 30 days; leave it out to receive only new ones.

**Scope:** `wc_webhooks:manage` · **Idempotency-Key:** optional

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key returns the first answer (kept 24 h). Leave empty in Try it: a new one is made for every call.

url.description: Your HTTPS endpoint (port 443, public host). Record POSTs each event here and counts any 2xx as the acknowledgement

backfill_from.description: Also deliver events from this time on (at most 30 days back)

201.description: The endpoint (the existing one when this URL was already registered)

status.description: auto_paused: Record stopped sending after 20 failures in a row. Fix the endpoint, then PATCH status active

existing.description: true when this URL was already registered: nothing new was created

400.description: `VALIDATION_FAILED`: the URL is not a public `https://` address on port 443.
